issue: Minor echo: 'rak kayu ini hari ini' stacks two 'ini' — grammatical and understandable, just slightly clunky read aloud. 'rak kayu itu hari ini' would flow better.
'menaiki tangga' is written-register; across a table people say 'naik tangga'. Full meN- form is policy-canonical (rule 5), so acceptable, but naik is the lexicalized everyday verb here.
'masih berfungsi' leans technical-manual; the across-the-table phrasing for grandma's sewing machine is 'masih bisa dipakai' or 'masih jalan'. Not wrong, slightly stiff for the domestic scene.
'Jalan menuju bandara' has a travel-notice flavor (menuju); casual speech says 'jalan ke bandara'. Situationally defensible as reported closure info.
English gloss calques the membuat+passive frame: 'Strong winds made the flight to Lombok get postponed' is not natural English. Indonesian sentence is fine.

fix.english: Strong winds caused the flight to Lombok to be postponed until tomorrow morning.

issue: 'orang tua' is ambiguous (parents vs. the elderly). The contrast pair 'orang tua dan anak kecil' does read as 'old folks and small children' in a health warning, so it works, but a learner who just learned orang tua = parents may misparse. 'orang yang sudah tua' would be unambiguous.

Tip factual error: glosses the root 'putus' as 'decide'. Putus means broken/severed/cut off; the verb 'decide' is memutuskan. As written the tip teaches a wrong word meaning. Sentence itself is excellent.

fix.grammar: ke-...-an also makes nouns from verbs: memutuskan decide, keputusan decision; sempat manage to, kesempatan chance.

issue: Collocation: friendships 'berawal dari', not 'mulai dari'. 'Persahabatan kami mulai dari kos yang sama' is clipped and off-collocation — mulai dari is the 'starting from/ranging from' frame, not 'originated in'.

fix.target: Persahabatan kami berawal dari kos yang sama lima belas tahun lalu.

issue: Loose topic-comment pivot: 'Kebiasaan kecil ... lama-lama terasa hasilnya' switches subject midstream (the habit ... its results are felt). Genuinely conversational Indonesian does this, so it passes — but it is at the edge.

Elliptical 'kalau' doing 'in case' duty: the full spoken chunk is 'untuk jaga-jaga kalau mati lampu'. Also 'mati lampu di jalan' is a slightly odd frame (mati lampu prototypically = building/neighborhood outage). Understandable, mildly compressed.

Site vocabulary: workers say 'lokasi proyek' (or 'proyek' alone) for a construction site; 'lokasi pembangunan' is planning-document language. Tool/PPE vocab (helm, sarung tangan) is otherwise precise; wajib register fits a safety rule.

fix.target: Helm dan sarung tangan wajib dipakai semua pekerja di lokasi proyek ini.

issue: 'hilang arah' — standard form is 'kehilangan arah' (or plain 'tersesat'); bare 'hilang arah' is attested colloquially/poetically but is the marked choice.

Weather-vocab precision: 'surut' prototypically describes tides/floods receding; a well running low is usually 'mengering' or 'airnya menyusut/berkurang'. 'Air sumur surut' is attested and understood — minor precision ding.
Set idiom clipped: 'dibahas panjang' — the fixed collocation is 'dibahas panjang lebar' (discussed at length). Bare 'panjang' reads as truncated.

fix.target: Usul yang kamu tulis kemarin dibahas panjang lebar dalam rapat direksi tadi pagi.

issue: Orthography: 'lebaran' lowercase. Lebaran is a proper noun (the holiday) and is capitalized — the deck itself writes 'Lebaran' in its three other occurrences, so this card breaks internal consistency too. Sentence and perantauan tip are otherwise excellent.

fix.target: Setiap Lebaran, rumah kami penuh dengan saudara yang pulang dari perantauan.

issue: Dictionary-example-ese: 'sinyal telepon hilang' — nobody says sinyal telepon; it's 'sinyal HP' or just 'tidak ada sinyal'. The bare-sinyal version is the natural remote-area complaint.

fix.target: Peta kertas tetap berguna kalau tidak ada sinyal di daerah terpencil.
fix.english: A paper map is still useful if there is no signal in a remote area.

issue: 'rambu peringatan' — rambu is prototypically road signage; beach warning boards are 'papan peringatan'. Rambu-rambu is used loosely enough that this passes, but papan would be the precise pick.

'gelombang tinggi akan berlangsung sampai' — berlangsung suits events; forecast-speak (BMKG) is 'berpotensi terjadi hingga' or plain 'masih tinggi sampai'. Acceptable news register for a forecast sentence.

'kini' is written/reflective register; neutral speech uses 'sekarang'. In a capstone dulu-vs-kini contrast sentence it is defensible (rule 4 latitude), but it is the only baku-flavored word in the card.

The tail 'kalau kamu masih berminat' logically conditions the telling, not the opening — an FYI frame. Spoken Indonesian genuinely does this and the English mirrors it, so it passes, but strictly the kalau-clause dangles.

Proverb variant check: card gives 'Sekali mendayung, dua tiga pulau terlampaui' — the dominant modern/textbook form. Classical peribahasa dictionaries have 'Sekali merengkuh dayung, dua tiga pulau terlampaui'. The short form is what Indonesians actually quote, so it stands as canonical-in-use; noting the variant for the record. Usage sentence and tip are clean.

Proverb wording off: canonical form is 'Buah jatuh tak jauh dari pohonnya' — the fixed proverb uses 'tak', and normalizing it to 'tidak' breaks the quoted wording (severe under proverb-exactness rule; a learner who repeats the card's version will sound off). 'tak' is already deck vocabulary via id-3930 'Tak kenal maka tak sayang'. Application clause and tip are good.

fix.target: Buah jatuh tak jauh dari pohonnya; anak itu rajin persis seperti ibunya.

issue: English gloss calques 'melahirkan': 'every answer gives birth to a new question' is translationese. Indonesian melahirkan = 'generate/spark' in this frame; the Indonesian sentence itself is natural and vivid.

fix.english: That child's curiosity never runs out; every answer sparks a new question.
